examples.knowledge_point: Solving for Unknowns By Computing a Product and Equating Real and Imaginary Parts
examples.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $1+2\textrm{i}$ to get rid of the fraction and isolate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & =\frac{p-2q\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}} \\ (2-3\text{i})(1+2\text{i}) & =p-2q\text{i} \\ 2+4\text{i}-3\text{i}-6{\text{i}}^{2} & =p-2q\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i}-6(-1) & =p-2q\text{i} \\ 8+\text{i} & =p-2q\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can equate the real parts and the imaginary parts separately.

- Equating the real parts, we get

$$
8 = p.
$$

- Equating the imaginary parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-2q \\ q & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=8$ and $q = -\dfrac{1}{2}.$

First, we equate the real parts:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & =a\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we equate the imaginary parts:

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =b\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a=\sqrt{5}$ and $b=6.$
